## Git Cheatsheet {.unnumbered}

A quick reference for every command in these lessons. Angle brackets like `<file>` mean "fill in your own value."

### The everyday rhythm

Most of your Git life is this short loop:

```bash
# before you start, get the latest
git pull origin main

# ... edit files ...

git add <file>            # stage your changes
git commit -m "message"   # save them to history
git push origin main      # send them to GitHub
```

Check in with `git status` any time you're unsure where things stand.

### One-time setup (per computer)

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `git config --global user.name "Your Name"` | Set the name stamped on your commits |
| `git config --global user.email "you@wisc.edu"` | Set the email on your commits (match GitHub) |
| `git config --global core.editor "nano"` | Use nano for commit messages (what these lessons assume) |
| `git config --list` | Show your current configuration |
| `ssh -T git@github.com` | Test that your SSH key connects to GitHub |

### Starting a repository

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `git init` | Turn the current folder into a Git repository |
| `git clone <address>` | Copy a GitHub repo onto this computer |

### The core cycle

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `git status` | Show untracked, modified, and staged files |
| `git add <file>` | Stage a file for the next commit |
| `git add <file1> <file2>` | Stage several files at once |
| `git add .` | Stage **all** changed files (run `git status` first!) |
| `git commit -m "message"` | Save all staged changes as a commit |

### Renaming and deleting files

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `git mv <old> <new>` | Rename or move a file, keeping its history |
| `git rm <file>` | Delete a tracked file (stages the deletion) |

Both still need a `git commit` to record the change.

### Seeing what changed

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `git diff <file>` | Changes since the last commit (not yet staged) |
| `git diff --staged` | Changes that are staged for the next commit |
| `git diff HEAD <file>` | All changes since the last commit |
| `git diff <commit> <file>` | Compare your file to a specific past commit |
| `git log` | Full commit history |
| `git log --oneline` | One compact line per commit |
| `git log --oneline <file>` | Only the commits that changed `<file>` |
| `git log -2` | Just the two most recent commits |

### Undoing and restoring

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `git restore <file>` | Discard uncommitted changes to a file |
| `git restore --source=<commit> <file>` | Bring back an older version of a file |
| `git reset HEAD~1` | Undo the last commit, keeping its changes in your files |
| `git stash` | Set aside uncommitted changes to return to later |
| `git stash pop` | Reapply the changes you stashed |

Name a past commit with `HEAD` (latest), `HEAD~1` (one before), and so on — or copy its ID from `git log --oneline`. Only `git reset` commits you have **not** yet pushed.

### Ignoring files

Create a file named `.gitignore` and list patterns, one per line:

```
*.tmp          # any file ending in .tmp
receipts/      # a whole folder
secret.env     # a specific file
```

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `git add .gitignore` | Track the ignore file so the rules are shared |
| `git add -f <file>` | Force-add a file that is being ignored |
| `git status --ignored` | Also list the files being ignored |

### Working with GitHub

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `git remote add origin <address>` | Link your local repo to a GitHub repo |
| `git remote -v` | Show the remotes you've connected |
| `git push origin main` | Send your commits up to GitHub |
| `git pull origin main` | Bring GitHub's changes down to your computer |

After your first `git push origin main`, bare `git push` and `git pull` also work — but naming `origin main` keeps it unambiguous.

### Key terms

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Repository (repo)** | A folder Git is tracking, plus its history |
| **Commit** | A saved snapshot of your project at a point in time |
| **Staging area** | Where changes wait after `git add`, before `git commit` |
| **HEAD** | The commit you're currently on (usually the latest) |
| **Remote** | A named connection to a hosted copy (e.g. on GitHub) |
| **origin** | The conventional name for your main remote |

### Where your work moves

```
working directory  --git add-->  staging area  --git commit-->  repository  --git push-->  GitHub
```
